correctness.rationale: The proof is reconstructed without depending on finite testing. Distinct primitive rotations have distinct (d-1)-prefixes because they have identical Parikh vectors. Thus any periodic factor of length d-1 determines its phase; circular minimal absences have length <= d. Prefixes n >= max(1,2d-2) contain every circular factor of length <= d-1. Any other MAW must be a periodic factor. At length d, the sole possible absent rotation at n=2d-2 has phase d-1; for longer MAWs, presence of the length-(L-1) prefix and suffix forces starting phase d-1 and L=n-d+2. The corresponding word is absent, with both proper extreme factors present, including d=1. The binary period 01101 at n=7 disproves a uniform one-step smaller threshold. Complete direct factor-set tests: 11747; independently constructed two-sided-context tests: 4567. No finite test substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: General minimal-absent-word algorithms (Pinho et al. 2009; Barton et al. 2014) do not state a periodic-prefix formula. Fici, Restivo and Rizzo (arXiv:1707.04450, Lemma 2) establish the stable circular antidictionary from a doubled period but do not give a unique moving boundary or an optimal prefix threshold. A 2026 indexed source gives the analogous endpoint phenomenon only for complete powers of periods made of runs with pairwise distinct symbols; that case is covered and explicitly excluded from the novelty claim as a special case. The present statement handles arbitrary primitive periods and all prefixes beyond a sharp universal length cutoff. Full text of the indexed special result was inaccessible, so priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: The theorem is a natural all-alphabet, all-primitive-period structural classification for minimal absent patterns in highly repetitive strings, with a sharp universal stabilization threshold. It identifies every absent minimal pattern, proving that exactly one periodic boundary obstruction changes for all sufficiently long partial or complete repeats and that the cardinality stays constant. This is not a narrow arbitrary table or a special-case reparameterization: the known distinct-run result handles only a structured subclass, while this result treats every primitive root and an optimal cutoff. It supports compact antidictionary descriptions for long repeated texts, while explicitly excluding any unsupported measured performance claim.
